conventions.convention: The Seifert pairing is V(x,y)=lk(x⁺,y); the positive normal n satisfies that (n,u,v) is ambient-positive for a surface-positive tangent basis (u,v). Consequently V−Vᵀ is the surface intersection matrix.

Integral Seifert lattices have even rank and unimodular skew part. Rank zero is allowed, with empty determinant 1. A metabolizer is a primitive direct summand of half rank on which the entire bilinear pairing vanishes.

Rational isometric structures have even rational dimension, nonsingular symmetric B, invertible B-isometry T, and invertible I−T. Their metabolizers must be T-invariant. The definition permits the t+1 primary component.
For nonsingular integral V, the associated rational pair is B=V+Vᵀ and T=V⁻¹Vᵀ.
Positive Hopf-band boundary linking is +1, giving core self-pairing −1 in the positive-push convention. The selected ordered plumbing cores have intersection +1 and V₁₂=0.
The two classifications are abstract group isomorphisms; countably many copies mean direct sums, not products, and no equality of the integral group with the rational group is asserted.
The surjection theorem assumes full AC and uses smooth oriented endpoint knots in both categories; TOP annuli are locally flat and have product end collars.

load_bearing.statement: A rational isometric structure consists of an even-dimensional rational vector space, a nonsingular symmetric form B, and an invertible B-isometry T with I−T invertible. Metabolic structures have invariant isotropic half-dimensional subspaces; direct sums with metabolic structures set to zero define G_Q.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Every integral 2g×2g matrix V with det(V−Vᵀ)=±1, including the empty matrix, is exactly the positive-push Seifert matrix of a connected compact smooth oriented surface in S³ with one boundary component and an ordered integral homology basis.
For every integral Seifert lattice (H,V), the class represented by (H,−V) is the additive inverse of the class represented by (H,V) in G_Z; full AC is assumed when the form comes from a knot.

Both elementary enlargements E₀(V;x,y,z) and E₁(V;x,y,z) of an integral Seifert matrix are integral Seifert lattices representing the same element of G_Z as V; full AC is assumed for knot-derived matrices.
Under full AC, the stated standard positive two-band plumbing has right-handed trefoil boundary and positive-push matrix [[−1,0],[−1,−1]] in the specified positive handle basis.
Assume full AC for the knot Seifert-pairing convention. For an invertible integral Seifert matrix V, B=V+Vᵀ is nonsingular, T=V⁻¹Vᵀ is an invertible B-isometry, and I−T is invertible.
Assume the full Axiom of Choice for knot Seifert pairings. Each of G_Q and G_Z is abstractly isomorphic to the direct sum of countably infinitely many copies of Z, Z/2Z, and Z/4Z.

Assume full AC. In both the smooth and locally flat topological concordance categories of smooth oriented knots, assigning the integral Seifert class of any connected oriented Seifert surface defines a surjective group homomorphism to G_Z.

concerns.concern: The Statement defines a positive Hopf band solely as 'an oriented annulus whose two boundary components, with their induced orientations, have linking number +1.' This omits the unknotted-core condition. A framed annulus around a nontrivial knot can satisfy this linking condition. Knotting the b-annulus away from the plumbing square and the specified disk for a⁺ preserves the stated linking/intersection conditions and matrix calculation, but does not justify the trefoil boundary identification in Proof 1.1. The later word 'standard' needs an explicit restriction consistent with the initial definition. The conventional missing condition is explicit in Quach Hongler–Weber, §2, printed p. 137: [The link of an extrovert divide](https://www.numdam.org/article/AFST_2000_6_9_1_133_0.pdf). Thus the definition and trefoil identification appear overbroad as written, although the displayed matrix follows from the other specified conditions.

Fact F7 states 'Linking of disjoint oriented curves is the signed intersection with a spanning two-chain' and cites thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection. That supplier's Statement instead requires a supplied compact embedded smooth spanning surface, transversality, and a regular diagram. The fact strengthens the cited interface without explaining the chain extension. Proof 2.1's actual cross-ball vanishing follows immediately from the homological linking definition because a curve bounds an integral chain in its ball, so this does not undermine the surjection.
